note: Primary fixture alias for #85050. On Windows, every claude start (interactive, -p, and --resume) spends ~75 seconds in two completely silent startup phases — nothing written to --debug while they run. Faceplate: preheating.
title: [BUG] Windows: ~75s of silent, unlogged startup phases (ending at '[skills] idle' / '[ScheduledTasks] scheduler start') - persists with skills removed, MCP disabled, nonessential traffic off
expected: Startup should log each phase. A trivial -p haiku Reply OK should not sit ~75s in two unlogged voids.
actual: Two large debug gaps: ~59.7s between Org fast mode: enabled and [skills] idle; then ~38.4s until [ScheduledTasks] scheduler start() — enabled=false, hasTasks=false. Same two-gap structure (~57–60s + ~17–38s) every run. After the second gap, rest of startup completes in ~1s.
knockOn: claude -p --resume of 8.7 KB session ~130s; 44 MB session 5.4 minutes. Interactive resume looks hung; users abandon.
ruledOut: Working-directory choice irrelevant. stdio MCP ruled out via --strict-mcp-config.
asks: if network/proxy then aggressive timeouts / opt-out (nonessential traffic flag did not help)
hypothesisNonBinding: Silent gaps may be network/proxy/VPN or config-hydration work that logs nothing; empty config bypasses them (6s). Verify nothing — encode measurements only. Do not invent runtime source claims.
